BREAKTHROUGHS.Definition: important new discoveries that greatly improve what we know or can do

BOASTS.Definition: has, as something impressive to be proud of

DIABETES.Definition: a disease in which the body cannot control the amount of sugar in the blood

ALZHEIMER'S.Definition: a disease of the brain, mostly in older people, that slowly destroys memory

DEMENTIA.Definition: a serious illness of the brain that causes loss of memory and clear thinking

FOR THE ABSENCE OF DOUBT.Definition: to make things completely clear (usually said “for the avoidance of doubt”)

DECEIVING.Definition: making people believe something that is not true

TIRELESSLY.Definition: with great effort and without stopping

NUTRITION.Definition: the study of food and how it affects health and growth

PEER REVIEW.Definition: the checking of a piece of research by other experts in the same subject before it is published

SAFEGUARD.Definition: something that protects against something bad

INTERROGATE.Definition: examine closely and ask difficult questions about

THOROUGH.Definition: careful and complete, with attention to every detail

SCANDALOUS.Definition: causing public shock and anger because it was seen as very wrong

DISPROVED.Definition: shown with evidence to be untrue

DISCLAIMER.Definition: a statement making clear what something is not meant to say

UPENDED.Definition: turned upside down; changed in a basic way

NEUTRINOS.Definition: extremely tiny pieces of matter with almost no weight that can pass through solid objects

CHEETAH.Definition: a large wild cat with spots that can run extremely fast

SUBATOMIC PARTICLES.Definition: extremely tiny pieces of matter, even smaller than the tiny units all things are made of

VACUUM.Definition: a space with no air or anything else in it

BACKYARD.Definition: done at home by people who are not experts

ARMCHAIR SCIENTIST.Definition: someone who talks confidently about science but has no real training or experience

FUNDAMENTALLY.Definition: in a very basic and important way

ANTICIPATED.Definition: expected and thought about in advance

BYWORDS.Definition: names that people use as typical examples of something

AGES.Definition: becomes out of date or seems wrong as time passes

DEFINITIVELY.Definition: in a way that is final and certain

CORRELATION.Definition: a connection between two things that tend to change together

NEWS FODDER.Definition: material that is easy for the media to turn into stories

NEWS OUTLETS.Definition: organisations that publish or broadcast news

METHODOLOGY.Definition: the set of methods used to do the research

EXTENSIVELY.Definition: in great detail and in many different ways

CHOLESTEROL.Definition: a fatty substance in the blood that can cause heart disease if there is too much

PRESS RELEASE.Definition: an official statement given to journalists

RAN WITH IT.Definition: eagerly published and spread the story

DUE DILIGENCE.Definition: careful checking of facts before acting
